PullRequest.Title: sessions: keep docked editor headers stable across tab switches
PullRequest.Body:
## Summary
Prevent the docked Details view from jumping when switching between Files and Changes in the Agents Window single-pane layout. Their shared header previously collapsed while context keys changed and menu actions were temporarily empty.

- Add an optional `reserveHeaderSpace` editor-group policy and wire it through the title/header controls.
- Reserve the header for docked editor inputs in the single-pane layout, independently of breadcrumbs and menu availability.
- Preserve existing behavior for Browser, ordinary editors, and groups without a custom header. No editor-input capability is added.

## Validation
- `npm run compile-client` passed.
- Hygiene passed for all eight changed files, including the pre-commit hook.
- Eight focused tests passed, covering tab switches with delayed menu updates at default/compact heights, opt-out behavior, and docked Details alignment.
- `npm run typecheck-client` passed.

## Manual verification
In the Agents Window single-pane layout, switch repeatedly between Files and Changes with Details visible. The header and Details top edge should remain stable while actions update. Open a Browser tab and verify it does not acquire an empty shared header.

Scenarios.Scenario: Switch between managed Files and Changes docked tabs in the Agents Window single-pane layout while header menu context updates asynchronously
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The existing active-editor event rebuilds header toolbars, computes visibility, synchronously relayouts the editor group, and then the existing group-relayout listener lays out the docked auxiliary bar. Delayed menu-item changes repeat the existing visibility/relayout path. The diff adds only a constant-time reservation predicate and keeps title height stable; it adds no new critical-path stage.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Synchronous DOM layout via editorPartContainer.getBoundingClientRect(), followed by editor pane and auxiliary-bar layout
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One downstream docked-auxiliary-bar layout per existing group relayout; active-tab and delayed menu events already caused these relayouts before the diff
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Active-editor and menu changes already called updateVisibility(true), EditorGroupView.relayout(), and the docked auxiliary-bar listener; the header could alternate between zero and 28/32 pixels when actions were transiently empty
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Runs synchronously during tab/menu UI updates, but the diff does not increase its invocation count and stabilizes the header height across the calls

Scenarios.ScalingInput: User tab switches and menu-context updates; one active group in this single-pane implementation, with no per-editor collection fan-out
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Serialized on the browser UI event loop; no added queue, parallelism, or concurrency burst
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No cache is read or populated on this path. Cold and warm behavior differ only in existing menu/context timing; the reservation check is the same constant-time instanceof test.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the event subscriptions, relayout call, downstream synchronous geometry read, and before/after visibility expression are directly traced.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact layout duration depends on editor and auxiliary-bar contents, but the diff does not add calls and should reduce geometry changes, so magnitude uncertainty does not support a regression finding.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable performance regression. The changed predicate preserves a 28/32-pixel header for two docked input classes and avoids the prior height oscillation without increasing relayout cardinality.

Scenarios.Scenario: Activate an ordinary editor, Browser editor, or empty group in the same single-pane editor part
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The existing active-editor event renders header actions and relayouts once. The reservation predicate evaluates false, leaving visibility controlled by breadcrumbs and menu actions exactly as before.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Existing synchronous editor-group and docked auxiliary-bar DOM layout
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One existing relayout per active-editor/menu visibility event; no collection scaling
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Header visibility followed breadcrumbs/actions and the same relayout path ran on active-editor changes
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Synchronous UI work remains on the event path, but the added false predicate does not add a boundary or increase frequency

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One active editor in the single supported group; cost scales only with existing editor/menu events, not the number of open tabs
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Serialized UI-thread handling with no new coalescing or concurrency behavior
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No relevant cache; the predicate is evaluated directly for the current active editor
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the policy returns false for non-DockedEditorInput and undefined, as shown by production code and focused tests.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Existing layout cost varies by editor content, but changed behavior for non-docked editors is only one constant-time type check.
Scenarios.Verdict: No regression: ordinary and empty-group header behavior is preserved with negligible constant-time policy evaluation.

Scenarios.Scenario: Create or recreate an editor title control during Agents Window startup or a show-tabs option change
Scenarios.CriticalPath: EditorGroupView passes the optional policy through EditorTitleControl into EditorHeaderControl. Existing header DOM, breadcrumbs factory, and toolbar construction remain unchanged; initial visibility evaluation gains one optional function call.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: One editor group in the single-pane part; recreation occurs on startup or relevant tab-option changes rather than per frame
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Synchronous, single UI-thread construction; no added async work or fan-out
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No cache or retained-key lifecycle is changed. The policy closure is held for the lifetime of the existing group/header controls and captures no growing state.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: constructor propagation and the only invocation site were inspected.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Startup frequency and exact toolbar construction cost are irrelevant to causality because those constructions predate the diff; only a constant-time predicate is new.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable eager-work, retention, or startup regression.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance review of all eight changed files and all diff pages. Traced editor activation, delayed menu updates, title-control construction, editor-group relayout, and docked auxiliary-bar DOM layout. The change adds a constant-time type predicate while preserving existing event and relayout cardinality; no subprocess, IPC, filesystem, database, network, cache-lifecycle, concurrency, or scaling regression was introduced, and no valid finding was submitted.
